A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ART-STVG research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary sections are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching content moved within v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ART-STVG benchmark results, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative and failure-case analyses in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds temporal-threshold ablation results in Table 9 and resource analyses in supplementary S4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same multimodal encoder, autoregressive cascaded decoders, spatial and temporal memory selection, and training losses. The newly documented temporal threshold and its ablation do not establish a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use HCSTVG-v2 and its LF-STVG-1min/3min/5min extensions for grounding experiments. The added resource analysis varies frame count but does not document a new grounding dataset, domain, or task; the hour-long storage calculation is not an additional accuracy evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator memberships in Tables 1, 6, 7, and 8 are unchanged. The new memory-scaling comparison in Figure 11 reuses TubeDETR, STCAT, and CG-STVG; it introduces no new comparison method or replacement of an existing comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds a threshold sweep over 0.7, 0.8, and 0.9 across the three LF-STVG benchmarks and GPU-memory profiling across frame counts extending to 23,000 for ART-STVG. These supplement the retained evaluation settings, including the original 64-frame efficiency comparison. Newly explained dataset construction does not establish revised experiments.

E4.justification: Supplementary S4 adds temporal-threshold sensitivity testing and analyses of memory scaling, memory-handling latency, and storage requirements. These are focused extensions to v1's existing component ablations and efficiency comparison. The original attention visualizations, failure cases, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The additional table and resource plot continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 and existing qualitative findings are unchanged. Table 9 adds threshold-dependent scores: on LF-STVG-5min, threshold 0.9 yields 14.4/9.5 m_tIoU/m_vIoU, while its 0.8 row repeats the existing 15.0/10.0 results. Figure 11 adds memory-scaling results, and S4 reports approximately 1% memory-handling latency overhead and a 22.5 MB history-storage estimate for 60 minutes.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and loss equations in Section 3 are unchanged. The added hyperparameter study and numerical storage estimate introduce no substantive formal definitions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: exploring LF-STVG, introducing ART-STVG with selective memories and cascaded decoding, and reporting strong long-form and competitive short-form performance. Wording changes do not materially alter these claims.

C2.justification: New S4 attributes lower-threshold degradation to redundant temporal context and higher-threshold degradation to excessive filtering of useful memories. It also expands the practical scalability argument using memory costs. Existing failure explanations and limitations concerning declining accuracy on longer videos and lack of real-time operation are retained, with limitations moved from S4 to S5.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future code-release promise with a repository address. Section 4 newly specifies randomized extension direction and duration and checks by three students for tube uniqueness and query alignment. S4 documents temporal-threshold choices and the float32 memory representation. These improve disclosure without establishing changes to the original implementation or dataset.

R1.justification: The same 54 bibliography entries and substantive positioning relative to STVG, long-video understanding, and autoregressive models are retained. Changed reference back-reference pages reflect document reflow rather than added or removed research.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording and grammar edits across the introduction, related work, experiments, and conclusion, and updates an author affiliation. It inserts supplementary S4 with three analysis subsections and renumbers the retained limitations section to S5, while preserving the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9 and Figure 11, enlarges Table 7 from a text-wrapped display to a full-width table, and relocates Figure 8. Existing figures and table contents are otherwise retained; these are localized presentation changes rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility documentation by specifying benchmark construction checks, temporal-threshold choices, and a code location. Table 9 and Figure 11 provide useful additional scrutiny of sensitivity and computational scalability while preserving the original evidence. The gain is limited: longer-video resource profiling adds no corresponding accuracy validation, latency measurement details remain sparse, and the new section contains unresolved references such as 'Tab. A' and 'As shown in Fig.'
